text: I have a call to order the regular schedule meeting for the Miami City Council  Tuesday, June 2nd, 2026 on to public hearing on proposed fiscal year 2627  budget. This public hearing is being called for any member of the public to  present to the governing body comments, recommendations, or information on any  part of the proposed budget. A public hearing on the proposed fiscal year  2627 budget. Is this my opportunity, Melissa? Yeah, will you declare it open? We'll declare the public hearing open.  Mayor, council members, city manager, and city attorney, my name is Wade. I am  speaking tonight as a concerned citizen on behalf of the other residents of  Miami who want accountability, transparency, and a budget process the  public can actually understand before major public money decisions are approved.  I want to be very clear at the beginning I am not here to accuse any employee,  elected official, or department of a crime. I am here because the city's own  agenda packet raises serious concerns that deserve answers before this  council approves the FY 2026-2027 budget resolution. Claims, contracts, and  related spending items. The first concern is this budget resolution itself,  section 2, appears to give the city manager authority to move unexpended  and unencumbered appropriations not only between line items, categories, and  departments, but also from one fund to another fund without further city council  approval. That is a very broad, in my opinion, too broad for a public budget of  this size. Enter fund transfers can change the real priorities of a budget  after the public thinks the budget has already been approved. I am asking  council to table this resolution or amend it tonight so that any material  enter fund transfer must come back to the council for public approval.  The second concern is that the general fund appears structurally dependent  on these transfers. The packet says 24.4% of the general fund, general  operations are being funded by transfers. That includes money from  the MSUA, capital improvement, workers' compensation, and unemployment. If the  general fund cannot balance without those transfers, the public deserves to see  that plainly. I am asking council to require a general fund without  transfer schedule before adopting the budget. The third concern is MSUA.  Utility customers deserve to know whether their electric water, wastewater, and  solid waste payments are being used only for utility purposes or also to prop up  other parts of the city government. The packet shows the MSUA transfers have  more than 14.7 million over a third of the MSUA budget. It also states MSUA has  nearly 2.85 million in past due debt, including recoverable, unrecoverable, and  written right-off debt. Before approving large MSUA transfers, I am asking  council to require a utility transfer schedule, a rate impact explanation, and a  debt aging recovery report. The fourth concern is claims transparency. I am not  saying that claims are improper. I am saying citizens cannot properly evaluate  public spending from summaries alone. The claims packet includes hundreds of  thousands of dollars in government claims, credit card charges, vendor  payments, professional services, equipment, and payroll. I am asking  council to require claims to be posted in a searchable format with invoice  numbers, purchase orders, purchase order numbers, departments, funds, contract  authority, procurement method, and whether each item was bid, quoted, sole  source, emergency, recurring, or grant funded. The fifth concern is public  safety technology. The packet references police cameras, Motorola equipment,  flock cameras, and guns. These are serious tools with serious privacy  and accountability implications. Before Miami expands license plate reader and  surveillance technology, I am asking council to require a written public  policy covering camera locations, data retention, search authorization, audit  logs, outside agency access, federal access, prohibited uses, misuse  penalties, and annual transparency reports. The sixth concern is outside support,  economic development sponsors, utility credits, waived fees, and  community support. I'm asking the  council to require annual reporting for MA, MAEDS chamber related  support, utility credits, sponsorships, fee waivers, and other  community support showing jobs created, jobs retained, private  investment, tourism impact, and housing impact and cost per  result. Finally, I am asking this council not to rush approval  simply because this packet is long technical. It's 244 pages I spent  my time on. My specific request is this. Table and  continue the FY 2026-2027 budget resolution until council  receives and publishes a revised transfer authority section  requiring public council approval for material interfund  transfers.
